name: Solenne Atelier Voidmarrow Couture Shroud
description:
A one-of-a-kind commission by Solenne Atelier's lead designer Mira Voss-Okafor, the Voidmarrow Shroud is constructed from hand-cultivated bioluminescent spider-silk analog grown in a controlled geneware substrate — each panel takes eleven weeks to produce. The base fabric is near-weightless, hanging in liquid folds of deep void-black that emit a cold blue-white inner light visible only in darkness. Embedded along the hem and cuffs are fragments of recovered deep-lake iron ore, polished and set as structural weights that give the garment its signature gravity-defying float-and-drop silhouette.

The rear panel accommodates decorative non-functional wings as a gene-compatible drape feature. No two Voidmarrow Shrouds are identical. This piece was commissioned for a Spire gala and has since been photographed in eleven corponation media feeds.
functionality: Bioluminescent panels activate in low-light environments. Iron ore hem weights create controlled drape physics that photograph distinctively. Gene-compatible rear panel drapes over decorative wing modifications without structural interference. BCI-responsive inner lining adjusts thermal output for climate comfort.
what_it_says: This person does not buy fashion — they commission it, and the world notices.
story_hooks: The Voidmarrow Shroud is reported stolen from a Spire penthouse — the owner refuses to involve CorpSec and is quietly hiring a private retrieval team.
A high-resolution image of the shroud contains a steganographic data payload embedded in the bioluminescent pattern — someone used the media coverage as a dead-drop.
Mira Voss-Okafor is approached to create a second Voidmarrow piece for a client she cannot identify — the commission offer is triple the original price.
